findings.current: The nomads who were left completely surrendered to us, and everyone in the Murong Family was either killed or captured.
findings.defect: The claim that everyone was killed or captured contradicts the later account of Murong Yeonghwi and several dozen others escaping.
findings.rationale: Preserves the reported victory without ruling out the fugitives established in Chapter 982.
findings.replacement: The nomads who were left completely surrendered to us, and the Murong Family’s forces were defeated.
findings.source: Chapter 980, Jin Taekyung reporting the victory

findings.current: The battle—and the war—ended that day.
findings.defect: An unqualified end to the war conflicts with Chapter 984’s announcement that the wider war has begun.
findings.rationale: Distinguishes the concluded northern campaign from the newly declared war against Dark Heaven.
findings.replacement: The battle—and the war against the invaders—ended that day.
findings.source: Chapter 981, account of the battle’s end

findings.current: If your innocence is proven in the future, the Murong family will have another chance to prove itself under a new Family Head.
findings.defect: The lowercase “Murong family” blurs the passage’s explicit distinction between the dissolved Murong Family and the surviving Murong household.
findings.rationale: Keeps the conditional offer aligned with the terminology established immediately before it.
findings.replacement: If your innocence is proven in the future, the Murong household will have another chance to prove itself under a new Family Head.
findings.source: Chapter 983, Namho’s offer to the survivors

findings.current: The man they would soon call their Family Head.
findings.defect: Treats Murong Su’s appointment as certain before the survivors’ innocence has been established.
findings.rationale: Retains the retainers’ expectation without prematurely resolving the condition Namho just imposed.
findings.replacement: The man they hoped to call their Family Head.
findings.source: Chapter 983, closing description of Murong Su

findings.current: Let it be known to all under Heaven, to all the people:
findings.defect: The displayed proclamation is left as unmarked prose rather than formatted as an ordinary quotation.
findings.rationale: Marks the document’s quoted opening without mislabeling it as a System panel.
findings.replacement: > Let it be known to all under Heaven, to all the people:
findings.source: Chapter 984, opening line of the imperial proclamation

summary: The packet is largely consistent, but two lines overstate how completely the conflict ended, one Murong passage resolves a still-conditional outcome, and the proclamation needs quotation formatting.
